hinglish.title: L-7.1: File System in Operating System | Windows, Linux, Unix, Android etc.
hinglish.why: Highest-viewed video in the entire Hindi File System series (1.29M views, 27.4K likes) and the natural entry point Gate Smashers' own playlist (L-7.1) uses before allocation methods and inode — sets up file concept/attributes cleanly before the numerical-heavy parts.

hinglish.title: L-7.6: Indexed File Allocation in Operating System
hinglish.why: Indexed allocation is the allocation method GATE numericals target most (block-pointer counting, index-block overhead); this lecture has the clearest worked example in the series and strong approval (13.2K likes / 460K views, comment thread shows students completing the full OS playlist from it).
comment_highlights: You are like "Jitu bhaiya" for CS students, Thanks
Completed the whole operating system series, Thanks for explaining every concept so beautifully.

hinglish.title: L-7.7: Unix Inode Structure with Numerical Example | OS
hinglish.why: The only high-quality Hindi video found with a full worked max-file-size numerical on UNIX inode direct/single/double/triple-indirect pointers — exactly the syllabus's named numerical topic — and comments show it is the final/near-final video of the well-regarded playlist (315K views, 7.2K likes).
comment_highlights: Finally completed the entire OS Playlist... took me 2 weeks along with note making (125 pages).
If someone is confused about the space taken by Inode & address pointers not counted!!!! Answer: because question was asked about...

runners_up.title: Free Space Management | Free Disk Space Management
runners_up.reason_rejected: Same series/quality as the two English picks and covers free-space management directly, but subtitles are disabled entirely on this video (youtube_transcript_api confirms no caption track) — fails the hard captions requirement.

runners_up.title: Directory Structure | tree structured directory | acyclic graph directory
runners_up.reason_rejected: Would be the natural English pick for directory structures (327K views) but subtitles are disabled — no caption track available.

runners_up.title: L67: File Allocation Methods | Contiguous, Dynamic Storage, Linked and Indexed Allocation
runners_up.reason_rejected: Titled/labelled in English and has auto captions, but the channel's own comment sections (Hindi-script jokes, a viewer asking 'Sir please give English subtitles' on the companion free-space video, other titles like 'UNIX Architecture | Explanation in Hindi') indicate the actual spoken delivery is Hindi/Hinglish, not English.

runners_up.title: L69: File Directories | Single-Level, Two Level, Tree Structural and Acyclic Graph Directories
runners_up.reason_rejected: Same channel/language concern as LWPMnCNd1q8 (Hindi-medium delivery despite English title); also a top comment complains the lecture just reads from the book.

runners_up.title: L68: Free Space Management | Bit-Vector and Link Approach
runners_up.reason_rejected: Same Hindi-medium concern; also very low engagement (only 12 comments pulled) and lowest view count of the three EEC candidates.

runners_up.title: L-7.3: Allocation Methods in operating system in hindi | Contiguous vs NonContiguous
runners_up.reason_rejected: Strong overview video (674K views) but overlaps heavily with the picked L-7.1/L-7.6/L-7.7 trio; excluded to stay within the 'up to 3 videos' cap in favour of the numerically richer indexed-allocation and inode lectures.

runners_up.title: L-7.4: Contiguous Allocation in Operating system
runners_up.reason_rejected: Good dedicated contiguous-allocation lecture (616K views) but not selected to respect the 3-video cap; contiguous allocation is the least numerically tricky of the three methods.

runners_up.title: L-7.5: Linked List allocation in file allocation with example
runners_up.reason_rejected: Solid linked-allocation example (509K views) but dropped for the same cap reason as L-7.3/L-7.4.

runners_up.title: Inode Structure
runners_up.reason_rejected: Genuinely English (Georgia Tech MOOC) and has captions, but is a short, general conceptual clip pulled from a heavily fragmented advanced-OS course, without a GATE-style worked max-file-size numerical — weaker fit than the Hinglish inode pick.

coverage_gaps: Hinglish: none of the 3 Gate Smashers picks has a dedicated free-space-management (bit-vector/linked-list) or directory-structure (single/two-level/tree/acyclic-graph) video — students should separately watch Gate Smashers L-7.2 (file attributes) plus a free-space-management video if needed. English: directory structures and free-space management are not covered at all by the two available picks — the only English videos found on those exact subtopics (Sudhakar Atchala's Directory Structure and Free Space Management) have no captions and had to be rejected, and no comparable-quality captioned/genuinely-English alternative was found; UNIX inode with a GATE-style max-file-size numerical also has no strong English match (Udacity's Inode Structure is conceptual only, listed as a weaker runner-up).
